name: BagBot Kraken Trader
tag: A command-line crypto bot for Kraken with clear strategy settings, paper mode and safety limits.

scenarios.title: Configure a strategy in paper mode
scenarios.ask: Set up a {strategy} strategy on a ${balance} paper balance with {size} per order.
steps: Wrote the settings file: {strategy}, ${=round(balance * size / 100)} per order, paper mode on.
Connected to sample price feeds for 3 trading pairs.
Set a stop for the bot if paper losses reach ${=round(balance * 0.1)} in a day.
Every simulated order and fee is written to a CSV log.
followups: How long should I run paper mode?
Long enough to see the strategy in calm and busy markets, often several weeks. Paper results still don't predict live results.
In a local environment file on your machine that is never committed or shared. Paper mode needs no keys at all.

scenarios.title: Switch to live mode safely
scenarios.ask: I want to go live with ${live} of real funds. Check my limits before switching.
steps: Checked that the API key has trade rights only and no withdrawal rights.
Daily loss limit ${=round(live * dailyloss / 100)}; largest order ${=round(live * maxorder / 100)}.
Live mode needs a typed confirmation and starts with the smallest order size.
One command cancels open orders and stops the bot.

result.title: Live preflight
rows: Crypto is volatile; you can lose money

followups: If the key were ever exposed, no one could move funds out of the account with it. It can only place and cancel orders.
What does the kill switch do?
It cancels all open orders and stops the bot. It does not sell your holdings unless you ask it to.

scenarios.title: Backtest a grid
scenarios.ask: Backtest a grid with {levels} levels spaced {spacing} apart over {days} days of sample data.
steps: Placed {levels} buy and sell levels covering a {=levels * spacing}% price range.
Counted about {=round(days * 3 / spacing)} simulated grid fills, including sample fees.
Summarized fills, fees and time spent outside the grid.

result.title: Backtest (sample)
rows: Past data doesn't predict future results

followups: Why does time outside the range matter?
When price leaves the grid, the bot stops trading or holds a one-sided position. A wider range lowers that time but spreads trades thinner.
Do fees matter at tight spacing?
Yes. At {spacing} spacing, each round trip must earn more than the fees on both sides. The report shows net results after fees.
